claims.claim: Chapter I: Mrs. Bennet tells her husband Netherfield Park has been let to a rich young man
claims.evidence: Netherfield Park is let at last? ... a young man of large fortune

claims.claim: She hopes he will marry one of their daughters
claims.evidence: I am thinking of his marrying one of them

claims.claim: Mr. Bennet teases her but agrees (to visit)
claims.evidence: Ch.1: 'I see no occasion for that'; 'It is more than I engage for'. Ch.2: he reveals 'I have actually paid the visit'
claims.fix: Mr. Bennet teases her and will not promise to call; in Chapter II he reveals he has already visited Mr. Bingley.

claims.claim: Mrs. Bennet has five daughters, wants them married
claims.evidence: a woman has five grown-up daughters; business of her life was to get her daughters married

claims.claim: Bingley takes Netherfield and falls for eldest, Jane
claims.evidence: Netherfield is taken by ... Bingley; 'preferred your elder sister to any other'
She is tolerable: but not handsome enough to tempt me

claims.claim: Elizabeth believes Wickham's lies about Darcy
claims.evidence: Wickham's account of the living and Darcy's treatment of his father's favourite

claims.claim: Elizabeth refuses Darcy's proposal; his letter shows her she was wrong
claims.evidence: scene 'I am not to be intimidated'/ letter chapters; later 'When I wrote that letter'

claims.claim: Visiting Pemberley she sees Darcy's better nature
Darcy secretly pays to force the marriage
claims.evidence: Mrs. Gardiner's letter: Darcy found them, 'His debts are to be paid... commission purchased'; 'must go no further'

claims.claim: Bingley returns and proposes to Jane
claims.evidence: Bingley, who wanted to be alone with Jane, proposed a walk; engagement follows

claims.claim: Lady Catherine tries to stop Elizabeth marrying Darcy, fails
claims.evidence: 'I am not to be intimidated into...' (Ch. LVI)

claims.claim: Elizabeth accepts Darcy; both couples marry
claims.evidence: 'Engaged to Mr. Darcy!'; 'rid of her two most deserving daughters'

claims.claim: Elizabeth: second of five daughters, quick-witted
claims.evidence: 'his second daughter'; 'Lizzy has something more of quickness'

claims.claim: Darcy: Bingley's friend, owner of Pemberley, Elizabeth's husband
Jane eldest, loved by Bingley; Lydia youngest
claims.evidence: 'the eldest Miss Bennet'; Lydia: 'youngest, I'm the tallest'

claims.claim: Wickham: officer who charms Elizabeth then runs off with Lydia
Mr. Bennet her husband, Elizabeth's father, ironic
